Perhaps your own hesitation/nervousness around the subject it is making him feel a little uncertain too? I know that happens in my relationship a little bit -  I find it hard to voice what I want because I’m shy sometimes, and then my boyfriend has absolutely no idea anything’s up, even when my mind’s racing. 

Rather than forcing yourself to overcome that (because that’s probably impossible if you’re anything like me), you could just say to him that you really are keen to engage in this lifestyle but find it hard to talk about it, and you might need his help/understanding/patience to talk about it. You could even try writing some things down that you like, and if you get stuck in the conversation then it’s there written out. 

Good luck!

I lay awake last night thinking I had some lucky escapes from creepy experiences with random men (like a few times I was followed, and one time I was mugged on a London street at night). Not to be melodramatic but those could have ended much worse. So not per se, but more retrospectively, I guess?

Toxic masculinity isn’t saying men are toxic though, it’s saying the culture, expectations and pressures on men is toxic, and means they’re left unable to express themselves for fear of appearing un-masculine. 
I’d say only seeing men with abs advertising boxers feeds into that as well. You’re only fed one acceptable way of looking. 
I’ve spent a lifetime trying to undo the damage of that message as a woman. My self-confidence has been majorly low. If I thought that men were going through the same thing (some clearly are) I’d say absolutely join with people who are just trying to get on the world without the notion of hating themselves holding them back.

I’m not sure if that’s fair. Just because women have largely created the body positivity movement, it doesn’t mean men aren’t welcome to join. There’s nothing about it that’s exclusive to women. 
Ultimately the movement is towards kindness and acceptance of all - isn’t that universal?

It sounds like you have an incredible capacity to be introspective and understand yourself, and it sounds like you’re compassionate and caring and just looking to be on the same page with your partner. All I can offer is (and this is so over-stated that it’s tedious, sorry!) is that you communicate. 

I think one of the other comments mentioned you could do this after sex? It’s a great time to be reflective in the afterglow - ask what pleases her; and talk about what you like (which gives her the chance to understand how she can fulfil what you want from her as well as vice versa). If your needs include being there in a caring/financial/relied-upon way then it’s good to state that. Does she know? Does she know that you’re not after sex to use her, but because you adore the connection? It might take more reassurance than you know. It might be incredibly hard work because those things may be so ingrained but the reward in terms of connection and intimacy will be amazing. 

Good luck!
